subject: Ephemeral latency offset request during DB cutover — hosted API p50/p95 measurement
messages:
From: Timothy Chen <timothy.chen@relicsight.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: devteam@relicsight.com
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short-term latency tolerance during DB cutover

Hannah,

Quick note from our ops team: we have a planned DB migration next Friday (10/15) that will cause a predictable spike in request tail-latency for a 90-minute window. Our SRE lead asked whether Redwood can provisionally accept a temporary adjustment to the hosted API p95 calculation for that window (we'd like a visible carveout or padding for that period).

We're not asking to change the contract permanently — just a one-off, time-boxed allowance (we can provide the migration schedule and runbook). We need to know:
- Whether Redwood can apply a temporary p95 padding or exclude the window from p95 aggregation for our tenant
- What evidence you would need post-cutover to demonstrate there was no customer-impacting regression
- Any pricing/credits or SLA implications we should expect

Attaching our cutover schedule and a short runbook.

Thanks,
Timothy Chen
Ops Lead, RelicSight
(attachment: relicsight-cutover-window.xlsx)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Chen <timothy.chen@relicsight.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term latency tolerance during DB cutover

Timothy —

Thanks for the heads up and for sending the schedule. We can support a time-boxed approach, but want to be explicit about the mechanics so both sides have the same expectations. High-level proposal from Redwood:

1) Window carveout vs. padding: we'll offer a provisional padding on p95 (an additive latency buffer) for the 90-minute migration window rather than removing the window entirely from p95 aggregation. Padding avoids blind spots in monitoring while giving you breathing room.

2) Measurement window semantics: the platform will mark all requests for your tenant with a "cutover" tag for the specified timeframe. For billing and SLA dashboards we will present both: a) standard p50/p95 computed normally, and b) p95_with_padding where we add a configurable buffer (we recommend starting at +200ms).

3) Evidence and rollback: we need two things post-cutover — (A) a short evidence CSV with per-minute request counts and error rates (we'll provide a template), and (B) an incident summary if any customer-visible errors occurred. If no customer-visible regressions are observed, the provisional padding will be journaled and will not affect your contractual SLA.

4) Credits & pricing: because this is operationally bounded and anticipated, we do not plan to apply usage credits. If the cutover causes sustained SLA breaches outside the window or increased support effort, we'll revisit credits case-by-case.

Next steps I propose: Ben will draft the formal carveout configuration and Marissa will prepare the evidence template and newline instructions. Can you confirm the exact start/end timestamps (including timezone) and whether any beta routes will be excluded?

I'll attach the provisional plan we use for these cases (PDF).

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-provisional-offset-plan.pdf)

From: Timothy Chen <timothy.chen@relicsight.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: devteam@relicsight.com
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term latency tolerance during DB cutover

Hannah —

Thanks, that approach sounds workable. Confirming the migration window: 2026-10-15T22:30:00-07:00 to 2026-10-15T24:00:00-07:00 (90 minutes). We'll exclude internal-only beta routes; production traffic only. We'll use the evidence template you mentioned — can you send it over now so we can pre-populate?

Also: our procurement team asked whether the padding value can be negotiated down from +200ms if Redwood's telemetry indicates good steady-state behavior during the first 30 minutes. In other words, can we have an automated rollback of the padding if p95 signals look stable?

Tim

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Chen <timothy.chen@relicsight.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term latency tolerance during DB cutover

Timothy — good questions. 

I've uploaded the evidence-template.csv and a short automation runbook to the shared Drive link (see thread metadata). Quick answers:
- We'll provision a p95_with_padding metric set to +200ms by default.
- We can enable an automatic rollback rule: if p95 (raw) stays within 10% of your 7‑day baseline for a 30-minute sliding window after cutover start, we'll reduce padding to +75ms and then to +0ms if stability holds for another 30 minutes. This will be an opt-in rule you must confirm; we will not trigger rollback without an explicit config flag in the carveout request.
- We'll mark the window in your account audit log and include a time-stamped entry in the monthly SLA report.

I've attached the evidence template and a one-page config snippet. Please reply with the confirmed timestamps and whether you want the automated rollback opt-in.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference
(attachments: evidence-template.csv)
